overview.headline: Presidential election cycle from primaries to inauguration

keyPoints.point: Presidential election happens every four years in November on a set Tuesday rule.
keyPoints.quote: An election for president of the United States happens every four years on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November.

keyPoints.point: The process of electing a president spans almost two years of steps.
keyPoints.quote: The process of electing a president takes almost two years.

keyPoints.point: States and parties hold presidential primaries and caucuses before conventions.
keyPoints.quote: States and parties hold presidential primaries and caucuses.

keyPoints.point: Electors cast votes for president in the Electoral College in December.
keyPoints.quote: Electors cast their votes for president in the Electoral College.

keyTerms.gloss: Contests where parties hold votes to choose presidential candidates
keyTerms.quote: States and parties hold presidential primaries and caucuses.

keyTerms.gloss: Local party meeting where debates take place to review candidates
keyTerms.quote: Primary and caucus debates take place.

keyTerms.gloss: Group where electors cast votes for president after November
keyTerms.quote: Electors cast their votes for president in the Electoral College.

keyTerms.gloss: Gatherings where parties choose presidential candidates for the next stage
keyTerms.quote: Parties hold nominating conventions to choose their presidential candidates.
